report.title: Branch operations, borrowed views and payload factoring in Either
report.explanation: For either 1.19.0 with default features on x86_64, is_left/is_right identify the actual branch; left/right return the corresponding optional payload; left_or/right_or select that payload or the given default; flip swaps the branch and a separate composition theorem proves flipping twice returns the original value. left_and/right_and select the supplied value or preserve the opposite payload. factor_none moves the optional payload outside Either while retaining its tag. factor_first/factor_second move the common tuple component outside Either. as_ref preserves the variant and referenced value; as_mut preserves the initial view and its generated backward function writes a matching-variant replacement payload back to the original variant. The fourteen original bodies terminate normally in the model for all well-typed values in their stated domains.
report.trusted_assumptions: The Rust compiler, official Charon/Aeneas translation, standard-library models and Lean kernel are trusted. Transitive theorem axioms are limited to propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. No local helper contracts or custom models are assumed. Reference contracts use Aeneas's value and backward-function semantics; they do not independently verify the compiler borrow checker or Rust aliasing model.
report.limitations: Only the fourteen named methods and the two-flip composition are proved. Remaining inherent methods, callback-taking APIs, iterators, pinning, standard trait implementations and serde remain unproved. Rust destructor behavior and resource consumption are outside the pure value model. All-feature/no-default configurations and other targets were not proved.
report.environment: Original crates.io either 1.19.0 Rust files and Cargo.toml, archive-compared; default features, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu. Rust nightly-2026-09-17, Charon 08d7c9d50144bd84848212c24701253585e90d1f, Aeneas be86ab0f1989d04944292b345b24c435be3ad10a, Lean 4.35.0. The union of the fourteen roots is extracted once into one Generated module and proved in one Proofs module.

report.title: Exact integer generation, seed initialization and state restoration in Rand32 and Rand64
report.explanation: For oorandom 11.1.5, twelve unchanged APIs have exact value/state proofs: new, new_inc, state, from_state, the unsigned output method and the signed output method for both Rand32 and Rand64. For arbitrary seed and increment input, new_inc normalizes the stream to ((increment << 1) OR 1), starts at zero, performs one PCG state update, adds the seed modulo the state width, then performs a second PCG state update. new uses the published DEFAULT_INC. state returns the exact current state and increment, and from_state restores those values unchanged; two additional composition theorems establish save/restore identity. Unsigned generation returns the exact PCG-XSH-RR output permutation of the old state and advances to multiplier*state+increment modulo 2^64 or 2^128. Signed generation preserves that updated state and reinterprets the unsigned result bits as i32 or i64. Each covered call terminates normally in the Aeneas model for every scalar input, including zero states and even restored increments.
report.trusted_assumptions: The Rust compiler, official Charon/Aeneas translation, official Aeneas scalar models and Lean kernel are trusted. No custom external models or local trusted helper contracts are used. All fourteen public and supplementary theorem dependency audits permit only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Standard-library wrapping, casts, shifts and rotations use official Aeneas models, rather than body proofs of Rust std implementations.
report.limitations: The proof covers twelve integer/state APIs on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu with the original default configuration. rand_float and rand_range for both generators remain unproved, as do non-excluded inherited/default and external blanket methods. The save/restore composition theorem establishes pure state identity; no arbitrary user callback or destructor behavior is modeled. No period, statistical distribution, independence or cryptographic guarantee is established. Other targets were not checked.

report.title: Exact PCG construction, state access and stream normalization for four generator types
report.explanation: For rand_pcg 0.10.2, state returns the exact stored word for Lcg64Xsh32, Lcg128Xsl64, Lcg128CmDxsm64 and Mcg128Xsl64. For the three LCG types, stream returns the stored increment shifted logically right by one; from_state preserves the given state and stores increment=(stream<<1) OR 1, discarding the highest stream bit. Their new constructors normalize that increment and initialize state=((input_state+increment)*multiplier+increment), with state-width modular arithmetic. The multipliers are 6364136223846793005, 47026247687942121848144207491837523525, and 15750249268501108917, respectively. Mcg128Xsl64::new stores input_state OR 1. Each of these fourteen original APIs terminates normally in the model for arbitrary scalar inputs. The prior Lcg64Xsh32::try_next_u32 exact PCG-XSH-RR output/state theorem is also retained, for fifteen proved API bodies total. The selected original bodies have byte-identical official Aeneas translations under the default and serde feature configurations, so these body guarantees apply to both configurations; this does not verify the serde trait implementations.
report.trusted_assumptions: The Rust compiler, official Charon/Aeneas translation, official Aeneas scalar models and Lean kernel are trusted. No custom external models, source adaptations or local trusted helper contracts are used. All fifteen theorem dependency audits permit only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Wrapping arithmetic, shifts, casts and rotations use official standard-library models, rather than proofs of Rust std implementation bodies.
report.limitations: Coverage is limited to the fifteen named bodies, default or serde features, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu. Model states need not have odd increments: the getter theorem reports the logical shift for every modeled state, but no save/restore identity is claimed for an arbitrary even-increment state. from_state/new normalize the increment exactly as specified. Advance, seed bytes/from_seed/seed_from_u64, other random-output methods, byte-buffer filling, RNG callbacks/forking, manual Debug, serde and inherited/default/external blanket APIs remain unproved. The proof does not establish period, statistical quality or cryptographic security. Other targets and dependency feature combinations were not checked.
report.environment: Unchanged crates.io rand_pcg 0.10.2 Rust sources and Cargo.toml; original archive/hash checks, tests and regeneration comparisons retained in evidence. report.title: Exact single-bit reads, updates and out-of-range panics for all integer types
report.explanation: For bit_field 0.10.3, the unchanged get_bit and set_bit bodies are verified for all twelve signed and unsigned integer types on x86_64. Every in-range index reads the requested bit or sets/clears exactly that bit; other bits are preserved. set_bit returns a mutable reference to the updated integer, and subsequent writes through that reference update the original value. Every out-of-range index fails at the explicit assertion. All twelve BIT_LENGTH values equal the integer widths. Original Rust source and Cargo.toml are unchanged. The Lean proofs use twelve explicit, separately monomorphized size_of integer layout models; Kani independently checks the original methods, returned-reference behavior and layout values for arbitrary valid inputs.
report.trusted_assumptions: The official Charon/Aeneas translation and scalar models, Rust compiler, Lean kernel, and Kani/CBMC are trusted. Twelve executable models supply size_of for the twelve integer types, with x86_64 byte sizes 1,2,4,8,16 and pointer size 8. No model is provided for arbitrary other Rust types. Kani layout/formula checks and Lean bitvector models are a reviewed semantic bridge, not mechanically connected proofs of Rust standard-library layout in Lean. The pointer-sized theorems explicitly assume System.Platform.numBits=64. All mapped transitive axiom audits permit only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
report.limitations: Only get_bit, set_bit and the associated primitive BIT_LENGTH values are established. The get_bits/set_bits range methods, generic BitArray slice methods, downstream trait implementations, other targets and release extraction remain unproved. The out-of-range result describes the translated explicit assertion failure, not panic text or unwinding side effects. Kani checks valid-index original method behavior and layout; Lean separately proves invalid-index assertion failure. Kani and Aeneas use different Rust nightly versions. This is partial crate coverage, not a proof of all public APIs.

report.title: Exact native word outputs and state updates for all fifteen xoshiro-family generators
report.explanation: For rand_xoshiro 0.8.1, the unchanged native word-generating method of each of its fifteen generators returns Ok of the specified output scrambler and performs the exact documented word-state transition. Coverage includes SplitMix64, both xoroshiro64 variants, all three xoroshiro128 variants, and all three variants of each xoshiro128, xoshiro256 and xoshiro512 family. For 32-bit-word engines the native method is try_next_u32; for 64-bit-word engines it is try_next_u64. SplitMix64::try_next_u32 is also proved independently, including its distinct Mix4 output formula, for sixteen proved API bodies. Each theorem covers arbitrary internal words, including all-zero states, and establishes normal termination in the Aeneas model. Array-state representation theorems establish that the four-word and eight-word inputs cover every valid fixed-length engine state. Exact output formulas and resulting fields are defined independently of the generated Rust body in the output*/next* specifications. The selected original bodies have byte-identical official Aeneas translations under the default and serde feature configurations, so these body guarantees apply to both configurations; this does not verify the serde trait implementations.
report.trusted_assumptions: The Rust compiler, official Charon/Aeneas translation, official Aeneas array/scalar models and Lean kernel are trusted. No custom external models, source adaptations or local helper axioms are used. All sixteen API theorems and sixteen supplementary array/representation theorems have dependency audits permitting only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Standard shifts, rotations, wrapping arithmetic and array operations use official Aeneas models, rather than body proofs of Rust std implementations.
report.limitations: Only the sixteen named native-output bodies are covered, with default or serde features on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu. Other-width output projections/compositions, buffer filling, seed construction, state serialization/accessors, jump/long_jump, Seed512 APIs, manual Debug, serde and inherited/default/external blanket methods remain unproved. All-zero states are included in the exact step formulas; seed validity, nonzero-state invariants, full-period behavior, statistical distribution, independence and cryptographic security are not established. report.title: Base16 length calculations and formatting-error conversion
report.explanation: For base16ct 1.0.0, decoded_len terminates normally for every input slice. It returns Ok of exactly half the input length when that length is even, and Err(InvalidLength) exactly when it is odd. It examines length only, so this result does not validate hexadecimal characters. encoded_len returns exactly twice the input length without a panic when the length is at most usize::MAX / 2. The handwritten From<Error> conversion into core::fmt::Error always returns the formatting error value normally for either source error, intentionally discarding which error occurred. These are body proofs of the unchanged published APIs; the length proofs quantify arbitrary slice lengths representable in the model.
report.trusted_assumptions: The Rust compiler, official Charon/Aeneas translation, standard-library slice/scalar models and Lean kernel are trusted. The proofs add no local axioms or custom standard-library models. Transitive theorem dependencies use only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
report.limitations: Only decoded_len, encoded_len and From<Error> for core::fmt::Error are covered; Display formatting is not proved. Hexadecimal encoding, decoding, character validation, destination writes, allocation and encode_str's unchecked UTF-8 conversion are not verified. encoded_len behavior above usize::MAX / 2 is outside the proved precondition. Other targets, feature configurations and release overflow behavior were not checked.

report.title: Exact integer writes and misuse checks in NoHashHasher
report.explanation: For nohash-hasher 0.2.0 on x86_64 with std enabled or disabled, Default initializes the stored value to zero, Clone preserves state, and finish returns the stored integer. Each of the ten integer write methods stores the Rust conversion of its input to u64: unsigned values are widened and signed values are converted modulo 2^64. With debug assertions enabled, the first integer write succeeds and a later write fails its assertion. With debug assertions disabled, each integer write replaces the stored value. The generic byte-slice write always panics in both configurations. These are exact per-method state and result contracts over all inputs, proved from unchanged published Rust bodies.
report.trusted_assumptions: The Rust compiler, Charon/Aeneas translation, their standard-library models, and the Lean kernel are trusted. The checked theorems use no extra local axioms; their transitive dependencies are limited to Lean's propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.
report.limitations: Coverage consists of Default, Clone, ten integer writers, write, and finish in the stated debug/release configurations. The handwritten Debug formatter, inherited Hasher default methods, full trait-instance integration, custom Hash implementations, BuildHasherDefault, and HashMap/HashSet behavior are not verified. In particular, this does not establish that a custom IsEnabled type obeys the required single-integer-write Hash protocol. Other targets were not checked. The upstream no-std IsEnabled doctest refers to the std-only IntMap alias and does not compile; the no-std unit tests and proved method bodies pass. A supplementary clone_from theorem composes the actual clone body with the official standard-library default model and proves exact replacement by source; it is not an independent std-body proof or a separate published API claim.
report.environment: Unmodified crates.io nohash-hasher 0.2.0; x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, std enabled and disabled; debug_assertions true and false. report.title: Exact ASCII byte values and eleven character classifications
report.explanation: For ascii 1.1.0, as_byte returns the exact ASCII code for every valid AsciiChar. The eleven classification methods are correct for all 128 characters: digits are characters '0' through '9'; alphabetic is A-Z or a-z; alphanumeric additionally accepts digits; lowercase and uppercase accept a-z and A-Z respectively; hexdigit accepts 0-9, A-F or a-f. Graphic accepts byte codes 33-126 and printable accepts 32-126. Blank accepts space or tab; whitespace accepts space, tab, LF, CR and FF, rejecting vertical tab; control accepts codes 0-31 or 127. All twelve original bodies terminate normally in the model, including their calls to shared classification helpers.
report.trusted_assumptions: The Rust compiler, official Charon/Aeneas translation, standard-library scalar models and Lean kernel are trusted. Proofs split the complete finite AsciiChar type and use kernel-checked logical reduction and proved scalar arithmetic, without native-evaluation trust. The byte-code table contains each actual ASCII variant in code order. Transitive axioms are limited to propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound; no custom models or local axioms are introduced.
report.limitations: Only the twelve named APIs are verified. Input validation, conversion from arbitrary bytes/chars, case conversion, AsciiStr, AsciiString, allocation, serde and unsafe paths remain unproved. Invalid enum representations are outside the input domain. The original is_digit_strange_radixes test fails on the pinned modern Rust because char::is_digit panics at radix 0/1; the distinct is_digit API is not covered. Remaining original tests pass with only that test excluded. All-feature/no-default configurations and other targets were not proved.
report.environment: Original crates.io ascii 1.1.0 Rust files and Cargo.toml, archive-compared; default features, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu. The upstream bindings_with_variant_name lint is disabled through RUSTFLAGS and corresponding official rustdoc doctest-build arguments, without source changes.
